searchText: for 8130, you have to register your authenticators with they keystore. for 8141 you need to update your wallet code. IMO those are pretty similar operations but are they? what if a smart wallet is not upgradable but allows arbitrary calls. works with 8130 but not 8141 if a smart wallet isn't upgradable yes, they wouldn't be able to use 8141 as written. that is a very small percentage of all accounts though one argument could be that if a smart wallet is not upgradable then it was intended not to have different authentication methods ^ yeah this is mostly my mental model if it is a problem we need to solve we could potentially modify the semantics of APPROVE i think it would be good to allow accounts to delegate to the default account also. which would address part of the concern above im not sure i get this. you mean a contract uses a 7702 (-like) delegation to a default account? yeah if you're EOA you can use 7702, if you're a smart account you'll (hopefully) be able to use eip-8298 setcodefrom soon an existing contract cannot call setcodefrom tho yeah they have to update their proxy impl now that i think about this more, allowing this sounds like a vulnerability. i know of a few contracts that are msig that by design can do whatever but are not allowed to change their own signers set and threshold for example wait also they can just DELEGATECALL to something the does SETCODEFROM
